narrative:
The model determined that you have a 32% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the loan amount you requested, the status of your checking account, and the purpose of the loan. The requested amount of 3,915 DM was the most important factor and worked in your favor, as it is not unusually large compared with what approved applicants typically request. However, this positive element was outweighed by the other two drivers.

Your checking account status of 0-200 DM pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk. Only 18% of approved applicants show this same modest balance level, while most maintain either no account or higher balances. Similarly, requesting the loan for business purposes also increased the perceived risk. Business loans are relatively uncommon among approved applicants (only 9% of approvals), and the model views this purpose as carrying higher uncertainty than more typical uses such as buying a car or furniture.

Taken together, these factors led the model to conclude that the overall risk was too high to approve the loan. 

To improve your chances next time, consider applying for a smaller amount, waiting until your checking account shows a stronger balance, and possibly choosing a different loan purpose. Strengthening these areas should help move future applications toward approval. (218 words)
